answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable credential issued only after an independent challenge, such as completing a randomly assigned task and passing a live liveness check. Credentials expire and are reissued unpredictably, so copying an identity or replaying old proofs does not multiply influence. An attacker must maintain distinct live agents and pay the real cost of each challenge, rather than minting names cheaply; a grove of umber bots chasing a comet of rewards still faces that bottleneck.
